query: What does the research say about the effectiveness of active learning approaches in undergraduate STEM courses?
research_brief: I want to understand what research says about the effectiveness of active learning approaches compared to traditional lecture-based methods in undergraduate STEM courses. Specifically, I am interested in outcomes such as student learning gains, retention rates, and overall academic performance. If available, I would also like to know whether certain types of active learning strategies (e.g., peer instruction, problem-based learning, group work) are more effective in STEM fields, and whether there are differences across disciplines (such as biology, chemistry, physics, engineering, etc.). Please summarize the key findings from recent primary research articles and meta-analyses, preferably with direct links to original journal publications. If research identifies limits or contexts in which active learning is more or less effective, please include those findings as well. I have not specified particular countries or institutional types, so all global or contextually varied research is acceptable.

think_reflections: This complex research question requires decomposition across multiple dimensions: (1) overall effectiveness of active learning versus lecture-based methods in undergraduate STEM in terms of student learning gains, (2) effects on retention rates and (3) on overall academic performance. Additionally, it asks about comparative effectiveness of active learning strategies (peer instruction, problem-based learning, group work), and (4) differences across STEM disciplines. (5) It also inquires about contextual factors or limits to effectiveness and (6) requests meta-analyses and recent primary study findings with links to sources. I will assign focused sub-agents to each of these angles. For each, keywords will focus on 'active learning', 'lecture-based', the relevant outcome or subgroup, and 'undergraduate STEM'.
